intent: To demonstrate the historical expansion and subsequent long-term stability of the number of countries possessing nuclear weapons.

requirements.question: Must the final 2015 value be explicitly stated as 9, or is the flat ending sufficient?
Is the full 1-to-10 expansion required, or is it enough to show only the final 9-country plateau?
Must the video explicitly identify 1990 as the peak, or can the peak be left implicit in the line shape?
Should the stability claim be anchored to 1995 (start of 9-country plateau) or to 1990 (last peak)?

units.claim: At the end of the series, in 2015, there are 9 countries with nuclear weapons.

basis.note: Final table row shows value 9 countries.

accept: In 2015, nine countries have nuclear weapons.
By the final year shown, the count is 9.
units.evidence: The 2015 data value must be readable as 9 countries at the end of the series.

units.claim: The number of nuclear-armed countries expanded from 1 in 1945 to 10 by 1990, an increase of 9 countries over that period.
accept: The count grows from 1 to 10 over 1945-1990.
Nine more countries acquire nuclear weapons between 1945 and 1990.
The series expands from a single country in 1945 to ten in 1990.
units.evidence: The series must show a clear rise from the 1945 value of 1 to the 1990 value of 10.

units.claim: The maximum number in the series is 10 countries in 1990; no later table year exceeds that value.
accept: The count peaks at 10 countries in 1990.
1990 is the highest point at ten countries.
The maximum is ten, reached in 1990.
units.evidence: The 1990 value must be visibly the highest point and readable as 10 countries.

units.claim: After the 1990 peak, the count falls to 9 by 1995 and stays at 9 for every later table year through 2015: a 20-year stable plateau with no increase.
accept: From 1995 through 2015, the number remains at 9 countries.
The count drops from 10 to 9 after 1990 and then stays flat for 20 years.
There is no increase in the number of nuclear-armed countries after 1990, with 9 countries from 1995 onward.
units.evidence: The 1995-2015 span must be visibly flat at 9 countries after the 1990 peak.

optional_valid: The 1955-1960 plateau at 3 countries and the 1970-1975 plateau at 6 countries.
Pakistan and North Korea first appear in the 1990 countries list.
The 1990 list contains 10 named countries: USA, Russia, UK, France, China, Israel, India, South Africa, Pakistan, and North Korea.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
